name: Red blood cell
headline: diameter
subtitle: Human
description: Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body and are the most common cells in human blood. A healthy one is a flexible disc that is thinner in the middle than at the rim, a biconcave shape that lets it squeeze through capillaries narrower than itself. Human red blood cells are about 7.5 to 8.7 µm across and 1.7 to 2.2 µm thick.

measures.label: Diameter
measures.note: Diameter of the normal disc-shaped (discocyte) human red blood cell

measures.label: Cytosol volume
measures.note: Volume of the cell's internal fluid, averaging 94 µm³ at 300 mOsmol/kg (1 µm³ = 1e-12 cm³)

measures.label: Diameter (rounded)
measures.note: Single rounded value listed by BioNumbers (from Rosen, Optimality Principles in Biology, 1967)

facts.text: Red blood cells can deform enough to pass through capillaries narrower than their own resting diameter.

sources.title: Shape and Biomechanical Characteristics of Human Red Blood Cells in Health and Disease (Diez-Silva, Dao, Han, Lim, Suresh, 2010)
Diameter of red blood cell - BNID 100798

caveats: NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls) pages returned a CAPTCHA and could not be read, so the dimensions come from a peer-reviewed review hosted on PubMed Central.
The 94 µm³ figure is the cytosol (internal fluid) volume, not a separately stated whole-cell volume; converted exactly from µm³.
